source_name: ZRSZ — Delavci v odpovednem roku (workers under notice) service page
why_relevant: Describes the employer obligation to notify ZRSZ of collective dismissals and the support programme for workers under notice. Documents the exact procedural trigger and timing (30 days ahead) that makes ZRSZ the earliest official touchpoint for a bank restructuring — essential for designing the collection cadence, and a candidate for FOI/statistical requests.

source_name: ZDR-1 art. 99 — Program razreševanja presežnih delavcev (statute text)
why_relevant: Defines the numeric thresholds (10 workers if 20–100 employed; one tenth if 100–300; >30 if over 300) that force an employer into a formal redundancy programme with union consultation and ZRSZ notification. These thresholds tell you exactly when a bank restructuring becomes publicly detectable versus when it can stay silent — a scoping rule for the whole cell.

source_name: SiStat / SURS — employment in financial and insurance activities (SKD K)
why_relevant: National statistical office database with employed/self-employed persons, labour costs and structural business statistics broken down by activity and size class; sector K (financial and insurance activities) is covered as a complete field. Provides the authoritative denominator for any headcount claim about Slovenian banking and a long back-series for trend work.

source_name: SURS StatWeb — news releases and methodological notes (plače, podjetja)
why_relevant: SURS first-release notes and methodological explanations (structural wage statistics, wages, enterprise demography) carry the narrative and definitions behind the SiStat tables, including for financial activities. Needed to interpret breaks such as the SKD 2008 to SKD 2025 change and to date releases correctly.

source_name: ZSDS — Združenje svetov delavcev Slovenije / ŠCID (works councils association)
why_relevant: The national association of works councils (svet delavcev), over 110 member councils, run through the Študijski center za industrijsko demokracijo in Kranj. Works councils hold statutory co-determination and information/consultation rights over status changes, mergers and headcount decisions — the second workforce channel besides unions. The site publishes recommendations, case articles and the Ekonomska demokracija material via its strokovniclanki subdomain.

source_name: Eurofound European Restructuring Monitor — Slovenia restructuring events
why_relevant: EU-level database of large-scale restructuring events, updated from national media, with roughly 487 Slovenian cases recorded and searchable by sector, type and date; includes historical banking cases (e.g. an NKBM job-cut case). Gives structured, comparable, already-deduplicated restructuring records for financial services — an aggregator that saves manual media triage.

source_name: Eurofound — Collective bargaining in Slovenia country profile
why_relevant: Structural reference on how Slovenian bargaining works (industry and company level in the private sector; national private-sector bargaining ceased end-2005). Provides the institutional frame needed to interpret whether a banking-sector dispute is sectoral or firm-level, and identifies the tripartite bodies involved.

source_name: UNI Europa Finance — sector federation news
why_relevant: European federation representing about 100 finance-sector unions and 1.5 million workers, running the BARSERVICE project specifically to strengthen collective bargaining in Central and Eastern Europe. Slovenian banking unions surface here in a European frame, and the federation publishes positions on digitalisation-driven job loss and branch networks that national unions later echo.

source_name: Delo — gospodarstvo/banking labour reporting
why_relevant: National daily that reports sector bargaining outcomes in detail — confirmed carrying the story that bank wages would not be indexed to inflation and that only Sindikat NLB signed the 2026 tariff annex while SBS refused. Often the first public record of which union signed what, since SBS itself has no visible news feed.

source_name: Večer — regional reporting on bank mergers and branch/staff impact
why_relevant: Maribor-based daily, strongest on the Nova KBM/SKB/OTP integration because of the Maribor headquarters question. Confirmed reporting on where roughly 2,500 OTP banka staff would work and which nearby branches would be merged — the concrete branch-and-headcount detail national outlets skip.

source_name: RTV SLO / 24ur — broadcast coverage incl. 'zapiranje poslovalnic' topic tag
why_relevant: 24ur maintains a keyword/tag page for 'zapiranje poslovalnic' (branch closures) that aggregates closure stories over time — a ready-made pointer feed for the branch-network dimension. RTV SLO covers ownership/merger completions such as OTP's takeover of Nova KBM. Broadcast outlets are usually where affected staff and local mayors get quoted.

source_name: Združenje bank Slovenije (ZBS) — branch opening hours directory
why_relevant: The bank association maintains a maintained list of branch working hours for banks and savings banks. Tracking this list over time is an indirect but employer-published way to detect branch closures and reduced-hours conversions before any redundancy announcement — the counterpart evidence to union claims.

source_name: OTP banka Slovenija — merger/ownership change Q&A and corporate notices
why_relevant: Employer-side primary source for the SKB/Nova KBM integration: the bank published a Q&A document on the ownership change and issues notices on branch mergers and account migration. Employer statements about 'optimizacija števila zaposlenih' in cases of duplicated roles are the official counterweight to union framing.

source_name: NLB Group — press releases and headcount disclosures
why_relevant: Largest banking group in Slovenia; press releases and periodic reporting disclose group headcount and branch counts and announce restructuring (a prior programme cut roughly 300 jobs, and a Slovak factoring unit closure cut 307). Employer-side ground truth against which union and ZRSZ signals are checked. Slovenian-language equivalent at nlb.si.

source_name: IUS-INFO — labour-law commentary on collective dismissals
why_relevant: Legal-publishing commentary explaining the collective-dismissal procedure (consultation with unions on redundancy criteria, ZRSZ notification, severance formula of one third or one half of average pay per year of service). Useful for interpreting whether a given bank restructuring was legally compliant and what documents must exist — which in turn tells you what to look for.

source_name: Sodna praksa (Slovenian case-law search) — labour and social court decisions
why_relevant: Public case-law database including VDSS (Higher Labour and Social Court) decisions. Dismissal disputes brought by bank employees reveal, with a lag, the internal facts of restructurings that were never announced — criteria used, numbers affected, whether the works council and union were properly consulted. A reveals-indirectly source with high evidentiary quality.

source_name: SeeNews - Slovenia Company News
why_relevant: SeeNews is the core SEE/Adriatic business wire and systematically translates Slovenian management-board and supervisory-board appointments into English short items (e.g. 'Intesa Slovenian unit appoints new CEO', 'Two supervisory board members of Slovenia's NLB take up office', 'Slovenia's bad bank names new executive director'). Highest-density single English channel for SI banking people moves.

source_name: SeeNews - Slovenia Politics News (regulator/central bank appointments)
why_relevant: Separate SeeNews desk that carries Banka Slovenije governor/deputy-governor and state-holding (SDH) appointment items which the company desk does not — needed for regulator-side org changes.

source_name: STA English service (english.sta.si)
why_relevant: The Slovenian Press Agency's English desk is the authoritative English rendering of Slovenian appointment news and the upstream that most foreign aggregators re-report; it also carries press-review items summarising what Delo/Finance wrote about bank leadership fights.

source_name: STA commercial wire portal (agency.sta.si)
why_relevant: The paid STA feed behind the English service; the place to negotiate structured, licensed access to the full appointment stream instead of scraping the free web front-end.

source_name: The Slovenia Times
why_relevant: English-language Slovenian outlet (STA-affiliated) that runs standalone stories on central-bank and bank leadership changes, e.g. 'Central bank under interim leadership' and 'Bank of Slovenia back with governor'. Good archival stability with numeric permalinks.

source_name: Total Slovenia News
why_relevant: English-language Slovenian news aggregator historically republishing STA business items, including corporate leadership changes, for an expat/foreign-investor audience; distinct keyword surface from local media.

source_name: bne IntelliNews - Slovenia
why_relevant: CEE/SEE business intelligence outlet covering Slovenian bank strategy and leadership in English, including the year-long central-bank governor vacuum and NLB's Addiko bid; adds context and named executives that short wire items omit.

source_name: The Paypers
why_relevant: Pan-European payments trade outlet that covers Slovenian PSP/processor news (verified item on Bankart partnering Nets for instant payments) and runs vendor appointment announcements that local Slovenian media ignore.

source_name: FinTech Futures - Slovenia region tag
source_subtype: fintech trade press with region tag + people-moves column
why_relevant: FinTech Futures maintains an explicit Slovenia region tag page and runs a dedicated people-moves/'appointments' stream for banking technology and fintech vendors — the closest match to the 'PaymentsDossier-style people-move column' this cell targets.

source_name: Finextra
source_subtype: fintech trade press + press-release wire + jobs board
why_relevant: Largest European fintech/banking news community; carries vendor and PSP press releases including occasional Slovenian bank technology and staffing announcements, and hosts a jobs board. Searches returned no Slovenia-specific people-move items, so treat as low-yield but broad-net.

source_name: IBS Intelligence (IBSi)
why_relevant: Banking-technology research house whose news desk routinely publishes vendor and bank-tech executive hires across Europe; useful for supplier-side (core banking, cards processing) appointments touching Slovenia that local press never covers.
